statement.excerpt: OpenAI will almost-certainly have to raise another round of funding by March 2027, likely at a similar scale to its $122 billion round from March of this year.
statement.locator: paragraph 68 of 188 (section 'How Does OpenAI Raise More Funding?')

from_speaker: will almost-certainly have to raise another round of funding
likely at a similar scale to its $122 billion round
With its IPO likely delayed — if it ever happens — until 2027
our_interpretation: We read 'almost-certainly' as high confidence about a definite outcome, which policy scores. The size clause ('likely at a similar scale') is hedged and is not scored.
We read 'by March 2027' as on or before 2027-03-31.
'Have to raise' is a forecast of need. Needing a round does not guarantee raising one, so a missing round alone would not contradict it.
We count a round as raised when OpenAI announces it and an investor discloses a signed agreement. Need can be shown by OpenAI's own statements or financial disclosures.
criteria.support_condition: By 2027-03-31, evidence shows that OpenAI needed another funding round, for example because it raised one and said it needed the money.
criteria.contradiction_condition: By 2027-03-31, evidence shows that OpenAI did not need another funding round, for example because its disclosures show it could cover its costs without one.
